# Oborodzuki portable benchmark

Double-click `Run-Benchmark.bat` from the development checkout. It finds the successful Renderer benchmarks workflow for the current branch head and checks both the Actions archive and portable ZIP against their SHA-256 digests. If GitHub requires authentication, use `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, an authenticated GitHub CLI, or the hidden token prompt. A fine-grained token needs read access to Actions in `amanosatosi/VSFilterMod_Oborodzuki`. The launcher fails if the artifact for the current commit is missing or expired.

For offline use, download the `oborodzuki-benchmark-windows-x64-<commit>` artifact from the matching [Actions run](https://github.com/amanosatosi/VSFilterMod_Oborodzuki/actions/workflows/benchmark.yml). Extract its inner `Oborodzuki-Benchmark-<commit>-windows-x64.zip` into a writable directory and double-click the included launcher. This explicitly runs that package's revision and verifies its file manifest. Keep the hidden `.github` directory when copying the extracted package. Use the development checkout launcher to discover subsequent revisions.

The package supports native Windows x64 and includes both compiled hosts, all renderer DLLs, fixtures, and the Python embeddable runtime. Windows supplies the system fonts. The reports list the real fixture's requested fonts that are absent from the Windows registry. Font fallback can differ across machines.

The single-worker suite uses five renderer paths. The scaling suite includes two alternating-order trials for the pinned baseline and candidate, plus full 5,400-frame KFX playback at each supported worker setting. Higher worker counts and full playback take longer. The pinned baseline's cap is eight workers. On a 6-core/12-logical-processor machine, the candidate also tests twelve. Each setting is checked on a separate overlap workload before timed trials. A particular scene may offer fewer parallel tasks than the configured worker budget. Mangetsu and Original VSFilterMod are descriptive references, with feature-dependent timings on the real ASS.

Each run opens its unique timestamped `Results` directory in File Explorer. Start with `summary.html` for charts or `summary.md` for tables. The CSVs include aggregate and individual frame times. `results.json`, `system-info.json`, `correctness-report.txt`, and `benchmark.log` record provenance and validation. The `raw` directory keeps host output, including sustained playback's frame hashes and timestamps. Press Ctrl+C to interrupt. Completed tests and available host output remain in the results directory.
